title: Closure and Dormancy Terms of the Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
Closing a Keyturn Host Payout Account runs to a notice period and a final sweep date set by the schedule, and an account left without activity for long enough is treated as dormant.

## Terms by schedule

| Payout schedule | Notice to close | Final sweep after notice | Dormancy period |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 7 days | 14 days | 540 days |
| Weekly Batch | 7 days | 14 days | 540 days |
| Express | 10 days | 14 days | 450 days |
| Instant | 10 days | 10 days | 365 days |
| Fleet Settlement | 30 days | 45 days | 730 days |
| Reserve-Backed Settlement | 45 days | 90 days | 730 days |

## The three periods

**Notice to close** is the calendar days' notice to close the account. **Final sweep after notice** is the calendar days after closure notice on which the final sweep runs. **Dormancy period** is the calendar days without activity after which the account is treated as dormant.

## Points of judgement

The two ends of the ladder are the furthest apart. A Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule account gives 7 days' notice, has its final sweep 14 days after that notice and is treated as dormant after 540 days without activity. A Keyturn Reserve-Backed Settlement Schedule account gives 45 days' notice, has its final sweep 90 days after the notice and is treated as dormant after 730 days. The Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule is the one schedule whose dormancy period is shortest, at 365 days, while its notice period of 10 days matches the Keyturn Express Payout Schedule.
